slides.label: Tensors Are Slot Machines For Measurement
slides.notes: Open with the chapter question rather than a component definition. A tensor is a device that accepts a prescribed list of vector and covector inputs and returns a number, vector, covector, or another tensor after operations. The route is slot type, component ledger, tensor product, contraction, metric duality, symmetry, and coordinate independence. Emphasize that the slots are the object; coordinates are only labels for reading the same machine.

slides.label: Valence Says What The Tensor Eats
slides.notes: Use the saved heatmap as a deliberately concrete ledger. The entries are not the tensor by themselves; they are the responses of the same multilinear machine when basis probes are inserted into its slots. Valence is the input contract. A covariant slot eats a vector. A contravariant slot eats a covector. The number of each kind predicts how many indices appear and where they live.

slides.label: Variance Keeps The Slots Honest
slides.notes: This slide slows down the upper-versus-lower index distinction. Lower indices correspond to vector inputs because one-forms measure directions. Upper indices correspond to covector inputs because vectors pair with covectors. The slot map is a bookkeeping discipline: when a coordinate basis changes, each slot transforms with the rule appropriate to what it accepts.

slides.label: A Linear Map Is Already A Tensor
slides.notes: Connect tensors to familiar linear algebra. A matrix for a linear map has one output direction and one input covector measurement, so it is naturally a mixed tensor with one upper and one lower index. The table changes with the chosen basis, but the operation v maps to A v does not. Ask students to name the two slots before they read the formula.

slides.label: Tensor Products Preserve Separate Slots
slides.notes: Explain tensor product as slot concatenation, not as mysterious multiplication. If alpha measures one vector and beta measures another, alpha tensor beta measures an ordered pair by multiplying the two independent readings. The component grid visual is the outer-product ledger. The important point is that the product creates a larger measurement machine before any summation or symmetry is imposed.

slides.label: Contraction Wires One Up Slot To One Down Slot
slides.notes: Contraction is the first operation that intentionally removes slots. Feeding a matching vector-covector pair through a dual basis and summing is drawn as a wire between opposite variance slots. This is why trace is the model example. The summation is basis independent only because the paired slots transform oppositely.

slides.label: The Metric Turns Vectors Into Covectors
slides.notes: Make metric duality visual before using the sharp and flat notation. The metric tensor evaluates two vectors, but fixing one vector leaves a covector that measures every other vector by length and angle against it. This is the musical isomorphism: the metric moves information between vectors and one-forms, and its inverse moves it back.

slides.label: Symmetry And Antisymmetry Are Slot Tests
slides.notes: Present symmetry as a behavior under slot exchange. A symmetric tensor does not care if two matching inputs are swapped; an antisymmetric tensor flips sign. Differential forms are antisymmetric covariant tensors, so they vanish on repeated directions and measure oriented area, volume, and higher directed pieces of geometry.

slides.label: Components Change; Measurements Do Not
slides.notes: This is the coordinate-independence checkpoint. A coordinate change redraws basis vectors and therefore changes the component table. But when the transformed components are paired with transformed input components, the scalar reading is the same. The slide should make the transformation law feel like protection for the measurement, not like a separate formula to memorize.

slides.label: Lab Ledger And Takeaways
slides.notes: Close by returning to the notebook evidence. The chapter artifacts give five ways to inspect the tensor story: valence, slot bookkeeping, component tables, product grids, and metric duality. The lecture ledger asks students to identify the object, the slots, the operation, and the invariant. The one-line takeaway is that tensors are coordinate-independent multilinear measurement machines with typed slots.
